To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) we propose a novel Generative Entity Networks architecture that disentangles entities and their visual attributes in a scene, (ii) the proposed architecture enables better generative models, (iii) the proposed architecture improves performance on natural language question answering.

we have developed a novel neural network model that jointly generates both images and their natural language scene descriptions, and that this representation enables a better generational model of images and also creates more semantically useful image representations.

we introduce Generative Entity Networks (GENs), which are a novel neural network model that can generate natural language descriptions of images and the images themselves, and which are able to disentangle the entities in the image from their attributes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of disentangling latent representations of visual scenes into entities and attributes.
developing a better understanding of the latent representations learned by generative models, and using them to improve the performance of such models in a variety of tasks.
the problem of disentangling the entities in a visual scene from their visual attributes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our work is the first to demonstrate the benefits of disentangled representations in a fully end-to-end generative image model.

we have shown that by using partial natural language descriptions, we can learn a disentangled representation of entities in visual scenes that is both more interpretable and more generative, and that this is possible without the need for explicit strong supervision of the entities.
the proposed model is a novel neural network model that can generate natural language scene descriptions and images of the described scenes, from a set of entities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to learn a disentangled latent space that can be used for generating images as well as answering simple questions.
we propose a novel model architecture that can generate high quality natural images from a set entities and their attributes, which can be described using natural language.

the proposed Generative Entity Networks can disentangle entities from their attributes in visual scenes using partial natural language descriptions and generate high quality images with the help of visual attention.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can improve the disentanglement of the latent representation of images by using partial natural language descriptions as a regularizer.
the ability of a model to disentangle the entities present in an image is critical for the quality of the representation it can learn, as well as for its ability to generalize to unseen entities.

the use of natural language descriptions can provide a strong prior on the latent representation, enabling the model to disentangle the entities in an image and learn a more interpretable representation.
